Connecting over Tor

AegisLink always connects through the embedded Tor, so your IP never reaches the relay. The first connection can take up to a minute. If your network blocks Tor, automatic mode tries bridges by itself (Snowflake, obfs4, meek); you can also pick one or paste your own in Privacy → Network → Tor connection.

relaySettings.title: My relay
relaySettings.previousUntil: Still receiving on the previous relay ({{relay}}) until {{date}}. Contacts who have not opened the app by then will need your new link.
relaySettings.ownDesc: Point AegisLink at a relay you (or someone you trust) run. Only Tor hidden services (.onion) are accepted: your IP is never exposed and no certificate is needed. Verify it first.
relaySettings.howToTitle: How do I run my own relay?
relaySettings.howTo1: You need a machine that is on when you want to receive (a small VPS, a mini-PC or a Raspberry Pi 4) with Docker. No public IP, no domain, no open ports.
relaySettings.howTo2: Get the AegisLink open-source code and run ./up.sh in infra/selfhost. It prints your relay’s .onion address.
relaySettings.howTo3: Scan the QR that up.sh prints (or paste the address below), tap Verify and switch. Keep a backup of the onion key: if you lose it, your address changes.
relaySettings.consequences: Your contacts will receive your new address automatically. For 7 days you keep receiving on the previous relay; anyone who does not open the app in that time loses your messages until you send them your link again. Your keys and chats stay on this device.
relaySettings.migrating: Registering on the new relay and telling your contacts…
relaySettings.done: Done. You are now on the new relay.

torConnection.title: Tor connection
torConnection.intro: AegisLink always connects through Tor and never over the normal internet. Here you choose how Tor reaches its network. If your network blocks Tor, a bridge disguises it as ordinary traffic.

modeSub.auto: Tries direct Tor and, if the network blocks it, moves on to Snowflake, obfs4 and meek by itself. Remembers what worked.
modeSub.direct: The fastest option when the network does not block Tor.
modeSub.snowflake: Connects through volunteers. Works on many censored networks.
modeSub.obfs4: Makes the traffic look random. Uses Tor Browser’s public bridges.
modeSub.meek: Looks like traffic to a large CDN. Slow, but gets through very restrictive networks.
modeSub.custom: Paste bridges you got yourself. They are harder to block than the public ones.

torConnection.customHelp: One per line. Get them at bridges.torproject.org or from the Telegram bot @GetBridgesBot. obfs4, webtunnel, snowflake and meek_lite are accepted.
